## TL;DR — DO NOT DELETE TONIGHT

Initial superficial check (`git diff --name-only main...$b`) **lied** because all three branches share **no merge base with `main`** — they are on disjoint history, and 3-dot diff returns empty when there's no merge base. Deeper inspection (`comm -23 <branch-tree> <main-tree>`) shows substantial unique content on every branch.

| Branch | Unique paths NOT on main | Last commit | Has remote? |

| `claude/migrate-packages-github-V2Ctr` | **861 files** | 2026-03-07 | no (local only) |
| `docs/s73-public-launch-planning` | **172 files** | 2026-03-18 | no (local only) |
| `public-release-cleanup` | **166 files** | 2026-03-17 | yes — `origin` |

**Recommendation:** **Review each branch in daytime, then archive-as-tag and delete** (`git tag archive/<branch> <branch> && git branch -D <branch>`). Do NOT delete until reviewed — there's substantive content here.

## What the Marshal would NOT do without a human

- Delete a branch with 800+ unique files. The cost of getting this wrong is irreversible loss of work.
- Push branch deletions to origin (destructive, public, observable).
- Cherry-pick across disjoint histories without manual review of every patch (high risk of conflict misresolution).
